sections.heading: Governance mechanism
paragraphs: Sacred relics carry religious meaning and may also require material conservation. Public access therefore works best when reverence is supported by provenance documentation, preventive conservation, controlled visitor movement, security, accessible interpretation and respect for local communities. These are governance principles, not reported details of this exposition.

sections.heading: Practical consequence and limitation
paragraphs: Such an event may broaden cultural access and strengthen awareness of Buddhist heritage, but these outcomes cannot be assumed from the announcement alone. Visitor pressure, commercialisation or inadequate conservation could undermine the heritage purpose.

advisory_notes: “from 31 October to 21 November 2026” is supported by the official title, but some reporting gives the final public display date as 20 November; preserve the official wording and avoid implying daily display at every venue.[1]
The note’s claims about tangible and living heritage are analytical definitions, not facts established by the PIB release; retain them as framing rather than event details.

“Cultural federalism,” “social cohesion,” “regional development,” and “cultural diplomacy” are reasonable UPSC lenses, but they should be presented as possible analytical dimensions, not demonstrated outcomes.

The claims about conservation, security, carrying capacity, commodification, over-tourism, and community participation are governance risks or recommendations, not reported features of this exposition.

The proposed GS1.1 anchor is appropriate for Buddhist heritage and religious-cultural practices; GS1.5 and GS2.6 are usable secondary links, but they are broader analytical connections rather than direct syllabus tags.
The pocketRead headline and deck accurately identify the event, but “public veneration” should not be expanded into confirmed universal or unrestricted public access without operational details.
The applied-question answer correctly labels the recommended safeguards as a proposed approach and accurately states that the supplied record does not establish operational arrangements.
The hypothetical exposition example is clearly labelled as an illustration and should remain so; its described safeguards must not be read as actual arrangements for Arunachal Pradesh.
